abstract: End-to-end path for a finished product ad built on FLUX 3. Covers endpoint-anchored shot design that survives generation, budgeting voiceover in the first generation round, phonetic screening of invented brand names, deriving cut points and spot length from measured speech rather than transcript timestamps, slipping each plate so its action lands on the spoken word that names it, requiring declared evidence for every line of on-screen copy, a cut and camera vocabulary that treats each shot relationship differently, deterministic manifest-driven assembly across ffmpeg and Remotion, and QC gates for the failures that pass every ordinary check: clipped audio tails, black frames in the body, products that hold identity while appearing to float, and claims that are on screen too briefly to read. Adds the failures that survive signal gates entirely: plates that arrive looking correct while depicting the wrong object, reference packs that mix two incompatible product designs across their angles, post steps such as clip reversal that move an action to the other end of a plate and silently invalidate timing derived before them, failed chain links whose stale output becomes the next link's input, and QC reports that record a pass the build did not give.
